# Pre Deployment Scripts - Technical Reference

> **📖 For usage instructions, see [README.md](README.md)**  
> This document contains technical reference information about the build process and contract details.

The repository includes a reproducible toolchain for pre-deploying canonical helper contracts. The workflow compiles the upstream sources deterministically, loads bytecode from a checked-in artifact, and provides a CLI for broadcasting deployments on L2 using pre-signed transactions.

## Contracts Included
- [Create2 Proxy (Arachnid)](https://github.com/Arachnid/deterministic-deployment-proxy)
- [ERC2470 Singleton Factory](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2470)
- [Create2 Proxy (Zoltu)](https://github.com/Zoltu/deterministic-deployment-proxy)
- [CreateX](https://github.com/pcaversaccio/createx)

> We deliberately left out Safe's singleton proxy, pcaversaccio's CREATE2 Deployer, and Multicall3 so their maintainers can keep publishing canonical addresses. Ping us once they report new deployments if you want to fold them back in.

A machine-readable summary of the compilation results lives at `artifacts/predeploy-bytecodes.json`; each entry exposes the deployment key used by the CLI, the bytecode, ABI (when applicable), compiler version, and language.

## Project Layout
- `contracts/vendor/` – vendored upstream sources preserved verbatim for auditability.
- `contracts/SingletonFactory.sol` – minimal ERC-2470 implementation used for compilation.
- `scripts/build-bytecodes.ts` – TypeScript script that compiles the sources (with the correct solc version per contract) into a single artifact file.
- `scripts/deploy-predeploys.ts` – TypeScript CLI for deploying on L1/L2 using ethers + zksync-ethers.
- `.env.example` – template showing the required environment variables.
- `package.json` – tracks runtime (`ethers`, `zksync-ethers`, `dotenv`, `commander`) and build-time (`solc`) dependencies.

> **Node version note:** `zksync-ethers@6.x` (and Hardhat tooling around zkSync) still expects Node.js ≥ 18.9.0. Running on Node 16 works for dry runs but will continue to emit warnings; upgrade before pushing real transactions.

## Setup
1. Copy the environment template and fill in your secrets:
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   # edit .env
   ```
2. Install dependencies (run once per environment):
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```
3. If you ever update the vendored Solidity/Yul sources, regenerate the deterministic bytecode bundle:
   ```bash
   npm run build:bytecodes
   ```
   The current `artifacts/predeploy-bytecodes.json` ships with the repo, so you only need this step after changing sources.

## Deployment

See [README.md](README.md) for complete usage instructions. The deployment script (`scripts/deploy-predeploys.ts`) automatically handles:
- Funding deployment addresses from your account
- Publishing pre-signed transactions
- Verifying successful deployment
- Reporting detailed status

## Contract Reference
| Key | Label | Compiler | Pre-signed Available | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `create2_proxy_arachnid` | Create2 Proxy (Arachnid) | `solc v0.5.8` | ✓ Yes | Minimal CREATE2 helper; salt in calldata slot 0, init code appended. |
| `create2_proxy_zoltu` | Create2 Proxy (Zoltu) | `solc v0.5.8` | ✓ Yes | Functionally identical bytecode to Arachnid/Safe version. |
| `erc2470_singleton_factory` | ERC2470 Singleton Factory | `solc v0.7.6` | ✓ Yes | Standard deterministic CREATE2 factory emitting `Deployed(addr,salt)`. |
| `multicall3` | Multicall3 | `solc v0.8.12` | ✓ Yes | Aggregate multiple read-only calls in a single transaction. |
| `createx` | CreateX | `solc v0.8.23` | ✗ No | Full-featured factory supporting CREATE, CREATE2, and CREATE3 flows. Bytecode included for reference. |


## Manual Deployment Steps

> **Note:** The automated script handles all of this for you. These steps are provided for reference or manual deployment.

To deploy manually:
- [Create2 Proxy (Arachnid)](https://github.com/Arachnid/deterministic-deployment-proxy): `0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C`
  - send 0.01 ETH (or equivalent in custom base token) to
      `0x3fAB184622Dc19b6109349B94811493BF2a45362` on the L2 network
  - then do

    ```bash
    cast publish  --rpc-url $L2_RPC
    ```

- [ERC2470 Singleton Factory](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2470):
  `0xce0042B868300000d44A59004Da54A005ffdcf9f`
  - send 0.03 ETH (or equivalent in custom base token) to
      `0xBb6e024b9cFFACB947A71991E386681B1Cd1477D` on the L2 network
  - then do

    ```bash
    cast publish  --rpc-url $L2_RPC
    ```

- [Multicall3](https://github.com/mds1/multicall/tree/main): `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11`
  - send 0.1 ETH (or equivalent in custom base token) to
      `0x05f32b3cc3888453ff71b01135b34ff8e41263f2` on the L2 network
  - then do
  
    ```bash
    cast publish  --rpc-url $L2_RPC
    ```

- [Create2 Proxy (Zoltu)](https://github.com/Zoltu/deterministic-deployment-proxy): `0x7A0D94F55792C434d74a40883C6ed8545E406D12`
  - Send 0.03 ETH (or equivalent in custom base token) to
    `0x4c8D290a1B368ac4728d83a9e8321fC3af2b39b1` on the L2 network
  - then do

  ```bash
    cast publish 0xf87e8085174876e800830186a08080ad601f80600e600039806000f350fe60003681823780368234f58015156014578182fd5b80825250506014600cf31ba02222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222a02222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222 --rpc-url $L2_RPC
  ```
